# Guttātherīgāthā (Thig 6.7)

**ID:** Thig 6.7
**Section:** Therīgāthā (thig)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Guttātherīgāthā* (Thig 6.7) is a poetic text preserved in the *Therīgāthā* collection of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. In these verses, the elder nun (*therī*) Guttā directly admonishes herself, warning against coming under the sway of her own mind (*citta*) [Devdas 2004]. The poem is available in multiple modern renderings, including English translations by Bhikkhu Sujato and Ayya Soma, and has been translated into at least ten languages [SuttaCentral].

The text of the *Guttātherīgāthā* is cited and explained in the commentary, the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, which shares extensive textual reuse with the poem across segments §0.3–7.1 [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral notes thematic and resembling parallels with verse collections focused on guarding the mind, including the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 153), two poems in the *Theragāthā* (Thag 1.78 and Thag 2.32), the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 31, Cittavarga), its Tibetan counterpart (Uv Kg 31), and several Chinese verse anthologies (T 210.19, T 212.32, and T 213.31) [SuttaCentral]. In addition, DharmaNexus automatically identifies cross-language text matches with the Chinese *Ekottarika Āgama* (增壹阿含經, T 125) and the Tibetan *Hevajra-nāma-tantrarājaṭīkā* (D 1188) [DharmaNexus].
